newsitem.title: USA: ValuJet Dec load factor below breakeven.
newsitem.headline: ValuJet Dec load factor below breakeven.

text.p: ValuJet Inc's load factor for December, three months after it resumed operations, improved about eight percentage points from November, but the low-cost carrier is still far from making money on its flights.
ValuJet said Tuesday its December load factor was 56.0 percent, down from 62.8 percent in the previous December but up from 48.2 percent in November 1996.
A ValuJet spokesman declined to say what would be needed to achieve profitabiity, but analysts agreed the carrier must add flights in order to make a profit.

"ValuJet's load factor is still 10 percentage points below the other carriers and certainly below its break-even load factor, which is probably still in excess of 100 percent," said Steven Lewins of Gruntal & Co.

"Given the fact that they have only 15 airplanes in the air and the U.S. has not certificated additional aircraft sufficient to service all of the routes that have been approved, they have a problem," he said.
In June, the Federal Aviation Administration grounded ValuJet's fleet of 51 airplanes after uncovering widespread maintenance problems.
The FAA scrutiny followed the crash of a ValueJet airliners in the Florida Everglades in June.
"I think it's pretty good that they did that well," said David Campbell of Scott & Stringfellow, commenting on the December figures.

"A lot of (negative) things happened that month -- the weather, the cut-back in their service. The company was hurt by delayed implementation of some of their new operations and all the confusion as to whether or not it was flying," he said.

In December ValuJet canceled all flights to Dallas and Fort Myers, stranding about 3,000 holdiay-season travelers. ValuJet cited a loss of confidence in the charter operator it had engaged to provide the service for the company. The FAA had refused to allow ValuJet to fly the routes itself, due to safety concerns.

Campbell said ValuJet also faced some tough competition in December from Delta Air Lines Inc, which matched ValuJet's fares. However, the low fares generated a lot of traffic that would not have been there otherwise, he added.

Asked what the company needs to make money, Campbell replied, "Just more capacity. They need a load factor somewhere around 51 percent on a system of about 30 aircraft -- just about double what they have now."
